subject: Argus Mission View cold-bootstrap recovery across retained event-log generations and concurrent rollover

findings.evidence: At public main 93a01f185f3c4800f127feca0739dbe7331c1950, _bootstrap_view still iterates only events.jsonl.1 then events.jsonl. event_log.py separately states that every generation is retained and event_log_paths() enumerates .2/.3/... then .1 then live in canonical oldest-to-newest order. Therefore a cold Mission View bootstrap can omit projected events that exist only in retained generations >= .2.
findings.scope: Cold bootstrap/recovery reconstruction only. This does not show normal online projection loses events.

findings.evidence: _tail_jsonl still reads at most the final 8 MiB of each selected file. Even within .1 or live, a projected event older than that tail is omitted during cold reconstruction.
findings.scope: Only event-sourced Mission View reconstruction; no claim about the canonical event log itself.

findings.evidence: tests/tools/test_event_log_query.py already constructs events.jsonl.2, .3, .1 and live and verifies iter_call_events returns them in oldest-to-newest order. Thus the repository already has a tested all-generation ordering primitive, but Mission View bootstrap does not use it.
findings.scope: This test validates event-log query ordering, not Mission View reconstruction or rollover snapshot atomicity.

findings.evidence: A fresh stdlib filesystem reproduction matching Argus rotation semantics started with .2=A, .1=B, live=C, enumerated those path names, then rotated .1->.3 and live->.1 and created live=D before opening all stored names. Reading the previously enumerated names returned A,C,D and omitted B although B remained durable as .3. Opening/pinning the three files before the renames and reading captured end offsets returned the intended A,B,C snapshot.
findings.scope: This is a deterministic source-shaped filesystem reproduction, not an observed Argus production incident and not an end-to-end execution of Argus Mission View code.

findings.evidence: JsonlEventSink._append takes events.lock and calls update_mission_view_event while still holding it; Mission View mutation takes mission-view.lock. snapshot_mission_view currently takes mission-view.lock only. A repair that acquires events.lock while already holding mission-view.lock would invert writer order and can deadlock. A safe cold-path design must avoid mission-view.lock -> events.lock inversion, for example by acquiring events.lock before mission-view.lock and double-checking bootstrap state, or by pinning event files/end offsets under the event lock before replay.
findings.scope: Constraint on a future repair; the current code does not itself acquire the inverted second lock.

findings.evidence: Public main is 15 commits ahead of the worker-observed 6953a117 source. _snapshot.py is unchanged across that range and fresh main still contains the two-file bootstrap. event_log.py changed only outside the relevant generation/rotation semantics. No matching public Mission View bootstrap issue was found in a repository issue search during this audit.
findings.scope: Absence of a discovered issue is not proof no private/unindexed report exists.

interpretation: clean-os-g1-006 is strongly supported as a concrete recovery-correctness defect and patch target. The source-level failure is simpler than a statistical headline: retained history and tested all-generation ordering exist, but Mission View cold bootstrap ignores generations >=.2 and truncates selected generations to 8 MiB. The additional rollover race is mechanically reproducible if a future implementation merely enumerates names and opens them later. The candidate should not be described as a proven production incident, and the proposed pinned-fd or lock-held repair has not yet been implemented and regression-tested in Argus.

confirmed: deterministic path-rebinding omission under matching rename semantics
preopened-descriptor snapshot preserves intended pre-roll files
not_confirmed: an observed production Mission View omission
frequency or user impact in deployed Argus
end-to-end Argus regression using concurrent writer/bootstrap barriers
correctness/performance of a specific proposed patch

recommended_decisive_tests: Add a Mission View cold-bootstrap regression with projected state only in events.jsonl.2/.3 and assert reconstruction includes it in canonical order.
Add a >8 MiB generation regression with a projected event before the old tail boundary.
Add a two-thread barrier test that forces rollover between snapshot selection and replay and asserts no retained generation omission and no deadlock.
Compare correctness-first events-lock-held replay versus preopened-descriptor/end-offset capture, preserving writer lock order and exact-once projection after the snapshot boundary.
reopen_condition: Reaudit clean-os-g1-006 when Argus changes Mission View bootstrap/event-log snapshot semantics, lands matching regressions, publishes a production incident/telemetry measurement, or provides a competing fix whose exact lock/snapshot behavior can be tested.
exact_next_action: On the next valid invocation, audit a different exact C24 identity row with independent numerical/raw-artifact leverage. Do not repeat clean-os-g1-006 unless the reopen condition fires; if selecting another Argus candidate, keep Mission View observability recovery separate from clean-os-g1-005 handoff authority/fencing.
